messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — private cluster 'acme-health-prod' autoscaler failed to provision requested GPUs. Queue growth >900 requests, sustained token throttling for customer routes. Notifying on-call. :rotating_light:

miguel (oncall): I'm on it. Paging eng-runtime and eng-sre. Any recent deploys to that cluster?

devon (support): Customer reports large batch job started ~10:12 UTC. They say latency spiked and requests started 503ing.

kevin (eng-runtime): looking at autoscaler logs now. Preliminary: cluster-autoscaler tried to create 8 nodes with label `redwood/gpu=true` but API returned quota/insufficient capacity errors. Logs: `Error creating instance: QuotaExceeded: Requested vGPU count exceeds quota`

jordan (eng-sre): pulling kube events & describe for pending pods.

jordan (eng-sre): `kubectl get pods -n acme-prod --field-selector=status.phase=Pending` shows ~420 pods Pending. `kubectl describe pod <one-pending-pod>` shows: "0/0 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taint {dedicated=gpu}:NoSchedule, 1 Insufficient gpu, 1 node(s) didn't match node selector"

kevin (eng-runtime): autoscaler attempted to scale group `acme-gpu-pool` from 2 -> 10. Cloud provider API returned `OperationFailed: Insufficient capacity in requested zone` for instance type `nvidia-a10g` and fallback types are restricted by customer's private cluster policy (only a10g allowed).

miguel (oncall): customer cluster is in Private mode (VPC, restricted SKU list). That explains why autoscaler couldn't pick other instance types. Need to coordinate with customer infra to allow alternative SKUs or wait for quota bump.

devon (support): Reaching out to AcmeHealth infra contact to confirm constraints and whether they can accept temporary SKU exception or manual node adds.

opsbot: Reminder: runbook `private-cluster-autoscale-failures` linked — steps 1-6.

miguel (oncall): Executing runbook step 2: scale down non-critical workloads and enable request-level fallback. Kevin, can we route critical traffic to hosted fallback for AcmeHealth until we recover?

kevin (eng-runtime): Yes. I can enable route override for their org-id and send critical inference calls to `hosted-gpu-fallback` pool. It will cost more but keeps SLAs. Doing it now.

kevin (eng-runtime): route override in place. Critical traffic for acme-org -> hosted fallback. Observability: request queue for that org dropped ~60% within 2m.

jordan (eng-sre): Manual provisioning attempt started: creating 4 nodes in `acme-gpu-pool` across available zones. Cloud API accepted 2 so far, 2 are stuck in `PROVISIONING` with error `Network interface creation timed out` — likely private subnet ENI limits.

miguel (oncall): That matches the customer's cluster constraints — limited ENIs per subnet. Devon, any word from customer?

devon (support): AcmeHealth reply: "we hit NodeGroup quota on ENIs and IPV4 addresses in the private subnet. We can increase, but it will take ~45-60m for infra team to open a ticket with cloud provider and for changes to propagate."

miguel (oncall): Ok. We'll continue mitigation: 1) keep hosted fallback for critical org traffic 2) pause non-urgent jobs on their cluster 3) attempt additional manual nodes in a different subnet if permitted. Kevin/Jordan coordinate with customer on subnet/ENI changes.

kevin (eng-runtime): Pausing incoming batch ingest for acme-org at the gateway. Also lowering concurrency limits via rate-limiter to reduce new allocations.

jordan (eng-sre): Trying alternative: create smaller instance flavors that still have GPU (a10g-compact) — but customer's policy denies that SKU. Filed request to operations to temporarily relax SKU whitelist.

miguel (oncall): Handoff soon — Sara will take over at 17:20 UTC. Summary before handoff: hosted fallback enabled for critical routes, manual nodes partially provisioned (2/4), autoscaler hitting capacity/quota + ENI limits, customer engaged and requested quota change (~45-60m). Current customer impact: severe for non-critical requests (throttled/queued), critical requests served via fallback with increased latency and cost.

sara (oncall): I'm here. Taking over from Miguel. Thanks for the notes. What's our target for restoring native cluster capacity?

jordan (eng-sre): If cloud/ENI quota increase completes within ETA, autoscaler should converge and remaining pending pods will schedule gradually. Otherwise we'll need to keep fallback and consider manual continuation of node provisioning in permitted subnets.

devon (support): Customer accepted temporary relaxation of SKU whitelist for two nodes to speed recovery, but internal security review may require justification. They requested a rollback plan after incident.

kevin (eng-runtime): Provisioning additional 2 allowed nodes with new SKU exception — cloud accepted. Now at 4/6 manual nodes healthy. Queue length trending down from 900 -> 220 over last 8 minutes. Token-level throttling reduced but still present for non-fallback traffic.

incident-bot: automated note — alerting channel `incidents` and paging logs captured under run `1769951123`.

miguel (oncall): quick blameless summary for handoff notes: root causes likely: (1) restriction of allowed SKUs in private cluster prevented autoscaler from choosing alternate instance types, (2) ENI/subnet resource limits prevented additional NICs, (3) cloud zone capacity shortage at scale request time.

sara (oncall): Action items captured: [kevin] keep fallback until capacity fully recovered, [jordan] follow up with customer on ENI/subnet quota increase and confirm cloud ticket, [miguel] start incident timeline + assign postmortem owner, [devon] update customer with ETA and rollback plan.

devon (support): Customer update posted: we've routed critical traffic to hosted fallback, working with Redwood/Cloud to add nodes; ETA ~45m to full native capacity; will confirm earlier if quota changes apply.

kevin (eng-runtime): Observability note: added temporary metric to flag SKU whitelist rejections so autoscaler errors show up in dashboards going forward.

jordan (eng-sre): Logs and relevant kubectl dumps saved to S3 at `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1769951123/`. Created cloud provider support case ID `CP-11872`.

sara (oncall): I'll keep monitoring. If we hit regression or customer impact grows, escalate to SOC and exec on-call. Otherwise continue with mitigation and schedule postmortem.

miguel (oncall): thanks team. Leaving a final note: avoid immediate config changes without customer approval in private clusters; prefer route fallback + targeted manual provisioning as first line.

devon (support): Customer acknowledged and appreciated the fast fallback.

sara (oncall): Marking this thread as active incident. I'll update `last_message_ts` when we close.

opsbot: Reaction :white_check_mark: on mitigation steps logged.
